description: §6.6.19 transitive limb — the hop's inner call sits inside a LAMBDA. Identical to the `-transitive` case in every respect except the call's POSITION, and that difference alone defeated the first implementation: its hop graph came from route inference's callee list, which returns at `case "lambda"` without descending, so `wrap` had no callees and the program compiled at exit 0 with an empty diagnostic set while binding an `async` fetch stub into the derived recompute.
rationale: §6.6.19 requires that 'reaches' mean a REFERENCE at any depth, including inside a lambda body, AT EVERY HOP — not merely inside the derived RHS. A hop graph and a reach check that disagree about what 'reaches' means are evadable exactly where they disagree, which is the S299 adversarial-review finding applied one level up. This case is the counter-gate for re-narrowing the hop graph to a call list: it pairs with `-transitive` so the two differ only in the inner call's position, making the regression unambiguous rather than a general 'transitivity broke'.
